questions.prompt: What does tamper-evident mean for a Content Credential?

options.text: The credential is locked, so that nobody is able to change the file at all
options.explanation: A credential cannot stop edits. It makes a change visible.

options.text: Any change to the file or the credential breaks the match, so it can be seen
options.explanation: Right. C2PA says even an insignificant change alters the hash, so the pieces no longer match.

options.text: The credential is hidden, so nobody can find it in order to change it later
options.explanation: The credential is not hidden. It is built so that changes show.

questions.prompt: What is a soft binding for?

options.text: It helps find a credential that was removed from the file, for example with a watermark
options.explanation: Right. C2PA says soft bindings let a credential be discovered even if it was removed from the asset.

options.text: It stops other people from copying the file, in the same way that DRM does it
options.explanation: C2PA says Content Credentials do not restrict access the way DRM does.

options.text: It replaces the hash, so the credential no longer needs a hard binding at all
options.explanation: C2PA says durable credentials combine a hard binding (a hash) with a soft binding. One adds to the other.

questions.prompt: An OpenAI check on an image returns a c2pa entry and a synthid entry. How do you read them?

options.text: Use only the c2pa entry, because the synthid entry is a result for audio files
options.explanation: Image results include both a C2PA entry and a SynthID entry.

options.text: Take the top-level outcome as the single final answer for the whole image file
options.explanation: The response has no top-level outcome.

options.text: Read each entry on its own, because the response has no single overall outcome
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to read each applicable entry in results independently.
